title: SOLIPSICON
narrativeSpine: Children dependent on harvested suffering and a human observer’s uncertain perceptions meet in a novel about hunger, identity and imposed experience.
firstSceneDraft: SOLIPSICON places vulnerable children above a world they are pressured to hurt.
Their own continued existence depends on machinery and rewards they cannot escape easily.
The philosophical science fiction also follows human experience from inside that pressure.
Its dual perspective complicates the boundary between a victim and an operator.
visualActionProposal: A failing dimensional nest folds around its child; a human clinic window reflects rain moving contrary to the actual exterior.
